issues.label: October 2026
issues.editor_note: Two big ACP trials (in JAMA and JAMA Internal Medicine) lead the month. A video decision aid in older adults with advanced CKD raised ACP documentation by 17 points and moved many patients toward conservative kidney management. EQUAL ACP found facilitated and self-guided ACP worked about equally well within Black and White groups, but facilitation looked relatively better for Black patients. On the pain side, a JSPM meta-analysis found no measurable benefit from adding acetaminophen to opioids, while NSAIDs looked helpful but with very low certainty. A systematic review of adjunct methadone is encouraging but rests on weak evidence.

papers.title: Video Decision Support and Advance Care Planning in Older Adults With Advanced Kidney Disease: The VIDEO-KD Randomized Clinical Trial
papers.authors: Volandes AE, Lakin JR, … Paasche-Orlow MK
papers.summary: Adults 65 years or older with advanced CKD at 12 clinics were randomized to usual care or a certified video decision aid. The video showed hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis and conservative kidney management, and patients then recorded their own goals-and-values statement, which was sent to their clinician. At 12 months, ACP documentation was 56.6% with the intervention vs 40.0% with usual care (difference 16.6 points, 95% CI 7.5–25.7). Documented discussion of kidney-failure treatment options was also higher (46.1% vs 31.6%).
papers.bottom_line: This is a scalable, low-touch tool that measurably increases ACP in the CKD clinic. After the video, far fewer patients were undecided (13% vs 41%) and about half preferred conservative management. This is worth raising with your nephrology colleagues.

papers.title: Advance Care Planning for Black and White Older Adults With Serious Illness: The EQUAL ACP Randomized Trial
papers.authors: Johnson KS, Ejem D, … Durant RW
papers.summary: Ten Southern US primary care and geriatrics clinics were randomized to lay-facilitated ACP (Respecting Choices First Steps) or self-guided ACP (Five Wishes) for seriously ill adults 65 years or older. Within each racial group, 1-year ACP completion did not differ significantly. For Black participants it was 71% facilitated vs 62% self-guided (aRR 1.15, 95% CI 0.83–1.59). For White participants it was 68% vs 78% (aRR 0.88). The race-by-intervention interaction was significant (aRR 1.32). Matching the facilitator's race to the patient's had no effect.
papers.bottom_line: Both approaches reached about 70% completion, but most of it was informal family conversation. Only 130 of 789 participants had new formal documentation. Facilitated ACP may matter more for Black patients, and racial concordance with the facilitator did not. See the accompanying commentary by Walling, Wenger and Sudore (JAMA, doi 10.1001/jama.2026.18377).

papers.title: Efficacy of Nonopioid Analgesics (Acetaminophen and NSAIDs) Used Alone or in Combination with Opioids for Cancer Pain: Latest Updates on the Evidence Supporting the Guidelines
papers.summary: This meta-analysis was done to update the Japanese Society of Palliative Medicine guidelines and covers RCTs through 2025, including IV formulations. Adding acetaminophen to opioids gave no significant improvement in pain (Hedges' g 0.18, 95% CI −0.08 to 0.44; 5 studies, n=253). Adding an NSAID to opioids showed a medium effect (g 0.58, 95% CI 0.07–1.09; 17 studies, n=1493), but heterogeneity was high (82%) and most studies had high risk of bias.
papers.bottom_line: The evidence for routinely adding scheduled acetaminophen to an opioid regimen for cancer pain is weak. An NSAID add-on is more defensible when there are no contraindications, though the certainty is very low.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Adjunct Methadone With Opioid Therapy for Cancer Pain: A Systematic Review
papers.summary: This is the first systematic review of methadone added to an ongoing opioid regimen, as opposed to a full rotation to methadone. It included 1 RCT, 3 prospective open-label studies, 5 retrospective studies and 4 case reports. Every study reported meaningful analgesic benefit. Adverse effects were reported in 10 studies, but few were severe.
papers.bottom_line: This supports a practice many palliative clinicians already use for poorly controlled or neuropathic cancer pain. The evidence base is mostly observational, so continue the usual QTc and drug-interaction precautions.

papers.title: Comfort and symptoms at the end of life with dementia in the Namaste Care Family cluster-randomised trial
papers.summary: This secondary analysis looked at Dutch nursing-home residents with moderate to advanced dementia who died during the Namaste Care Family trial. In the last week of life, discomfort (72%) and pain (70%) were common alongside serenity (80%). The program did not change symptom burden on the EOLD-SM or CAD scales. Staff found it hard to deliver the program in the last week of life.
papers.bottom_line: This was a negative trial. Sensory and engagement programs did not reduce last-week symptoms in dementia, and pain and discomfort remain common, so active symptom management is still needed.

papers.title: Pilot Study of Timely Integration of Interventional Pain Management for Advanced Cancer
papers.summary: Patients with advanced cancer, moderate to severe pain, prognosis over 6 months and modest opioid doses (≤200 MME) were referred early to a pain clinic for systematic consideration of procedures. 93% were seen within 4 weeks and 57% received at least one procedure. Those treated reported about 65% pain relief at 2 and 4 months, with improvements in pain intensity and interference. Quality of life was stable.
papers.bottom_line: This supports referring for nerve blocks and neurolysis earlier rather than waiting for high-dose opioid failure. Efficacy trials are still needed.

papers.title: Systemic anticancer therapy for refractory malignant bowel obstruction in advanced cancer patients: a retrospective cohort study
papers.summary: This single-center Paris cohort had inoperable malignant bowel obstruction refractory to medical management and received systemic therapy. The obstruction resolved in 33%, but 38% of responders re-obstructed after a median of 33 days. Median survival was 50 days, and 58% had grade ≥3 toxicity. Gynecologic primaries treated with first-line therapy did better.
papers.bottom_line: This is useful data for goals-of-care conversations about chemotherapy for MBO. About one in three resolve, toxicity is high and survival is short, with the possible exception of treatment-naïve gynecologic cancers.

papers.title: Heart Failure Medication Discontinuation Among Hospice Patients with Concomitant Heart Failure and Dementia
papers.summary: Among hospice patients with both heart failure and Alzheimer's or related dementias, 91–100% of HF medications were stopped at hospice admission. That included beta-blockers (97.5%), loop diuretics (97.0%) and RAAS inhibitors (94.1%). The rate was the same whether HF was the primary or a secondary hospice diagnosis.
papers.bottom_line: Almost all HF medications are stopped at hospice admission, including loop diuretics that may still relieve symptoms. Reconcile medications deliberately rather than by default.

papers.title: Does the way palliative care clinicians talk about delirium influence clinical care in the last days of life? A secondary analysis of qualitative interview data
papers.summary: In interviews with staff at two UK hospices, 'delirium' was rarely named. When it was, assessment and management decisions were more transparent. Terms like 'terminal agitation' or 'confusion' went along with a stronger emphasis on sedation. Hypoactive delirium was poorly recognized and seldom discussed.
papers.bottom_line: Naming delirium explicitly, including the hypoactive form, may push the team toward assessing it before reaching for sedation in the dying phase.

papers.title: When the Plan Must Change: A Qualitative Study of Communicating Opioid Deprescribing Decisions
papers.summary: The authors built and refined a framework for telling a patient on long-term opioids, who has developed opioid use disorder, that they need to switch to MOUD such as buprenorphine. They tested it with clinicians and people with lived experience. Six skills emerged: raise the concern directly, balance limits with shared decisions, express empathy, anchor the conversation in the ongoing relationship, counter stigma and preserve positive regard.
papers.bottom_line: A practical communication framework for an increasingly common conversation with long-surviving cancer patients.

papers.title: Transdermal Buprenorphine for Pain in Pediatric Palliative Care: A 23-Patient Retrospective Study
papers.summary: Children aged 8 months to 17 years, many with neurological impairment, were started on a 5 µg/h buprenorphine patch, and 43% needed titration. Pain control was rated good in 87%, alertness improved in 74%, and 13% had mild skin reactions. There were no serious adverse events. Sublingual buprenorphine was used for breakthrough pain in about a quarter.
papers.bottom_line: An off-label but well-tolerated option for children with low opioid needs or feeding difficulties.

papers.title: Laboratory Testing at the End of Life in Patients With Cancer: A Systematic Review of Utilization, Costs, Clinical Utility, and Patient Burden
papers.summary: In end-of-life cancer care, 68–97% of patients had lab testing, and use rose as death approached. Timely ACP was consistently associated with less testing, and hospice and palliative models often showed lower use or cost. Very few studies linked a test result to a change in management or a symptom benefit.
papers.bottom_line: Order a lab near the end of life only when there is a clear clinical question and the result could change management in line with the patient's goals.

papers.title: Survival Patterns Following Admission to Home-Based Palliative Care for Patients With Cancer: A 10-Year Cohort Study
papers.summary: In a Brazilian public home-based palliative program, PPS and cancer stage independently predicted survival. A PPS of 30 or lower meant markedly shorter survival, especially in the first 30–60 days. Liver and lung primaries did worst. A simple model of PPS plus tumor type performed as well as more complex models, though with modest discrimination (C ≈ 0.63).
papers.bottom_line: This reinforces PPS as the workhorse prognostic variable at admission. Discrimination is modest, so use it alongside clinical judgment.

papers.title: Racial Composition and Single-Input Dominance in the First Hospice Special Focus Program Cohort
papers.summary: This study analyzed the 50 hospices CMS selected in December 2024 for the Special Focus Program, which was later paused amid litigation. Selected hospices did have worse independent quality, measured by visits in the last days of life. They also served far more non-White patients (median 35% vs 17%), an association that held after adjustment and was driven by the share of Black patients. For 48 of the 50, a single algorithm input drove most of the score.
papers.bottom_line: Relevant to hospice oversight policy. The selection algorithm may unfairly target hospices serving Black communities, and requiring poor performance in two domains would have changed most selections.

papers.title: Palliative Care Physician Density and Other County-Level Factors Associated With Place of Death, 2021–2023
papers.summary: This is a brief report. US counties with more palliative care physicians per capita had a higher share of cancer and heart disease deaths occurring outside the hospital.
papers.bottom_line: Workforce data that support the case for palliative physician recruitment. The design is ecological, so it cannot show causation.

papers.title: Caregiving Relationships, Advance Care Planning, and Hospice Use in Later Life
papers.summary: Among Health and Retirement Study decedents aged 60 or older, hospice use did not differ by the type of informal primary caregiver. Compared with a spouse or partner as caregiver, it was lower for people with no identified caregiver (OR 0.46) and for those with only formal care (OR 0.62). Having a child or grandchild as primary caregiver was linked to slightly more ACP.
papers.bottom_line: Older adults with no identified caregiver are the group least likely to use hospice. Flag them for early palliative and hospice discussions.

papers.title: Models of palliative care for malignant disease in rural settings: Systematic review
papers.summary: Rural palliative models for cancer were mostly community-based and often used telehealth or hybrid delivery (11 of 18 studies). Some were specialist-led, others generalist- or navigator-led with specialist backup. Observational studies suggested benefits for symptoms and health-care use, while the two RCTs had mixed quality-of-life results.
papers.bottom_line: The most common working design is a hub-and-spoke model with specialist expertise embedded locally and telehealth support. Comparative and cost evidence is thin.

papers.title: Expert Agreement on Palliative Reasoning and Monitoring in Heart Failure: International Delphi Study
papers.summary: Heart failure and palliative care experts from nine European countries agreed on the steps of 'palliative reasoning' in heart failure. They also agreed on a monitoring instrument of 25 symptoms and 18 wishes-and-needs items.
papers.bottom_line: A consensus checklist that could structure palliative assessment in HF clinics.

papers.title: Added value of a specialized mobile palliative care team compared to the usual care in the primary care setting of Croatia: a 3-month prospective cohort study
papers.summary: Compared with usual care, patients followed by Croatia's home-based specialist palliative team scored better on person-centeredness, compassionate care, and physical and emotional functioning at 3 months. Their measured healthcare costs were lower, and more died in their preferred place (48% vs 23%). Loss to follow-up was high.
papers.bottom_line: Adds to the evidence for home-based specialist palliative care, though the follow-up losses weaken the conclusions.

papers.title: Acupuncture vs. Reflexology for Cancer-Related Pain in Palliative Care: A Pragmatic Study
papers.summary: Oncology patients chose 8 weekly sessions of either acupuncture or reflexology. Both groups improved within-group on fatigue, appetite and function. Only acupuncture improved ESAS pain, and only reflexology improved well-being and sleep. Patients chose their own therapy, so selection bias is likely.
papers.bottom_line: Low-quality evidence, but acupuncture may be the better integrative referral when pain is the main target.

papers.title: Development and Validation of End-Of-Life Indicators for Dialysis Patients: A National Consensus Study in Taiwan
papers.summary: Taiwanese nephrologists agreed most strongly (≥90%) on two end-of-life indicators for dialysis patients: prolonged mechanical ventilation with dialysis in an unconscious patient, and prolonged mechanical ventilation with multi-organ failure. Factor analysis identified three end-of-life subgroups: ventilator-dependent, critically ill and functionally dependent.
papers.bottom_line: These are high-specificity triggers for hospice and ACP referral in dialysis patients, mainly useful in ICU consult settings.
